fact: a discrete set of information resources organized for the collection, processing, maintenance, use, sharing, dissemination, or disposition of information
facts or ideas, which can be represented (encoded) as various forms of data; knowledge in any medium or form that can be communicated between system entities

the protection of information and information systems from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction in order to ensure confidentiality, integrity, and availability
preserving authorized restrictions on information access and disclosure, including means for protecting personal privacy and proprietary information
guarding against improper information modification or destruction and ensuring information non-repudiation and authenticity
the property that data has not been altered in an unauthorized manner, in storage, during processing, and while in transit
the quality that a system has when it performs its intended function in an unimpaired manner, free from unauthorized manipulation of the system
ensuring timely and reliable access to and use of information

the management, operational, and technical controls (safeguards or countermeasures) prescribed for a system to protect the confidentiality, availability, and integrity of the system and its information
required agencies to identify sensitive systems, conduct computer security training, and develop computer security plans; superseded by FISMA
established a Federal Chief Information Officer within the Office of Management and Budget to enhance the management and promotion of electronic government services
an individual or group within an organization responsible for ensuring that risk is viewed from an organization-wide perspective and managed consistently across the organization
the highest-level senior official or executive in an organization with the overall responsibility to provide information security protections commensurate with the risk
an organizational official responsible for designating a senior agency information security officer and developing and maintaining security policies, procedures, and control techniques
an organizational official with authority for specified information who establishes the policies and procedures governing its generation, collection, processing, dissemination, and disposal

an organizational official who carries out the CIO security responsibilities under FISMA and is the primary liaison between the CIO and authorizing officials; also known as the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)
a senior official or executive with the authority to formally assume responsibility for operating a system at an acceptable level of risk
an organizational official who acts on behalf of an authorizing official in the day-to-day security authorization activities, but cannot accept risk for the system
a senior organizational official with overall responsibility and accountability for the agency's implementation of information privacy protections
an individual, group, or organization responsible for the development, implementation, assessment, and monitoring of common controls (security controls inherited by systems)
an organizational official responsible for the procurement, development, integration, modification, operation, maintenance, and disposal of a system
responsible for ensuring that an appropriate operational security posture is maintained for a system; works in close collaboration with the system owner
responsible for ensuring that the information security requirements are adequately addressed in all aspects of enterprise architecture
an individual, group, or organization responsible for conducting system security engineering activities
responsible for conducting a comprehensive assessment of the security controls employed within or inherited by a system to determine their overall effectiveness
an individual, group, or organization responsible for setting up and maintaining a system or specific components of a system
an individual, group, or organization granted access to organizational information in order to perform assigned duties
examines systems to determine whether the system is meeting stated security requirements and organization policies, and whether security controls are appropriate
responsible for developing and enforcing appropriate physical security controls; in government, often processes personnel background checks and security clearances
responsible for ensuring that organizational procurements have been reviewed by appropriate officials
often the first point-of-contact for managers determining whether a security background investigation is necessary for a position; may handle security-related exit procedures
responsible for ensuring the provision of the services necessary for the safe and secure operation of an organization's systems, such as electrical power and environmental controls
responsible for maintaining a comprehensive privacy program that ensures compliance with privacy requirements, develops and evaluates privacy policy, and manages privacy risks
